record.original_question: Suppose a non-trivial classical knot K is modified by virtualizing some crossings so that the resulting virtual knot K~ is non-trivial and has unit Jones polynomial. Must K~ be non-classical, or could it still be virtually equivalent to a classical knot? More generally, if a virtual knot has unit Jones polynomial, is it equivalent to a classical diagram after virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization, and if one classical knot can be obtained from another by crossing virtualization plus virtual Reidemeister moves, must the two classical knots already be classically equivalent?

evidence.quote: Suppose the knot K is classical and not trivial. Suppose that K~ (obtained from K by virtualizing a subset of its crossings) is not trivial and has a unit Jones polynomial, V (K~) = 1. Is it possible that K~ is classical (i.e. isotopic through virtual equivalence to a classical knot)?
Suppose K is a virtual knot diagram with unit Jones polynomial. Is K equivalent to a classical diagram via virtual equivalence plus crossing virtualization?
Given two classical knots K and K', if K can be obtained from K' by a combination of crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, then is K classically equivalent to K'?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A virtual knot diagram is a generic immersion of a circle in the plane whose double points are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle around the double point). Two virtual knot diagrams are virtually equivalent if they are related by a finite sequence of the classical Reidemeister moves and the virtual Reidemeister moves (the "detour moves"). Crossing virtualization is the local operation that replaces a classical crossing by the same crossing flanked on two opposite sides by virtual crossings (equivalently, switching the crossing and surrounding it by virtual crossings). The Jones polynomial V(K) of a virtual knot K is the Kauffman-bracket Jones polynomial extended to virtual diagrams; one says V(K)=1 (unit Jones polynomial) if it equals the Jones polynomial of the unknot. A virtual knot is called classical if it is virtually equivalent to a diagram with no virtual crossings.

Problems.

(a) Let K be a non-trivial classical knot, and let K̃ be a virtual knot obtained from K by virtualizing some non-empty subset of its classical crossings. Assume K̃ is non-trivial and satisfies V(K̃)=1. Must K̃ be non-classical, or is it possible for K̃ to be virtually equivalent to a classical knot diagram?

(b) Let K be any virtual knot with V(K)=1. Must K be equivalent, via virtual equivalence together with applications of crossing virtualization (in either direction), to a classical knot diagram?

(c) Let K and K' be classical knots, viewed as virtual knot diagrams. If K can be obtained from K' by a finite sequence of crossing virtualizations and virtual Reidemeister moves, must K and K' represent the same classical knot (i.e., be classically equivalent)?
artifact.category_tag: Virtual knot theory and Jones polynomial
artifact.status_search_result: The questions appear in standard lists of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory. Partial results are known: virtual knots produced by virtualizing a single classical crossing of a non-trivial classical knot are known to be non-classical and to have unit Jones polynomial; however, the general questions (arbitrary subsets of virtualized crossings, the converse characterization of unit-Jones virtual knots up to virtual equivalence plus virtualization, and whether crossing virtualization plus virtual Reidemeister moves can identify inequivalent classical knots) remain open as of available sources.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory – Unsolved Problems (Fenn, Kauffman, Manturov)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems concerning virtual knots with unit Jones polynomial and their relation to classical knots via virtualization.
status_evidence.claim: These questions are recorded among the unsolved problems in virtual knot theory.

status_evidence.title: On a class of virtual knots with unit Jones polynomial (Kauffman, Dye, Silver, Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that virtual knots obtained by virtualizing a single crossing of a non-trivial classical knot diagram are non-classical and have unit Jones polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: the single-crossing virtualization case is settled, leaving the general subset case open.
